title: Everolimus + exemestane
context_label: Postmenopausal HR-positive / HER2-negative advanced breast cancer
schedule_summary: Usual starting doses are everolimus 10 mg once daily and exemestane 25 mg once daily; use the doses on your prescription. Both tablets are taken every day continuously. There is no planned rest week. Review benefit and tolerability over time; there is no fixed adjuvant completion date.
purpose: Exemestane lowers oestrogen production while everolimus blocks an intracellular growth pathway that can contribute to endocrine resistance. The aim in this setting is to control cancer and delay progression.
indication_text: Postmenopausal HR-positive/HER2-negative advanced disease after recurrence/progression following an NSAI, without symptomatic visceral disease. The intended endocrine partner is exemestane; do not automatically substitute another endocrine drug.
administration_text: Take everolimus at the same time daily, consistently with food or consistently without food. Take exemestane after a meal. Swallow tablets whole with water; do not crush or chew. If a dose is missed, take the next scheduled dose without adding an extra dose.
monitoring_summary: FBC, renal and liver profile; blood urea nitrogen and urinary protein. Blood glucose, total cholesterol and triglycerides; optimise pre-existing metabolic abnormalities. Review lung symptoms, infection, mouth health, all medicines, planned surgery/radiotherapy and exemestane bone risk. FBC, renal/liver profile, total cholesterol and triglycerides every four weeks or as clinically indicated. Fasting glucose as clinically indicated, with closer surveillance for diabetes or increased risk. At reviews assess mouth ulcers, intake, infection, cough/breathlessness, oedema, skin/bowel symptoms and adherence. Disease assessment and imaging follow the consultant plan; new symptoms can bring review forward.
review_status: Source reconciled; independent clinical, pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending

agents.name: Everolimus
agents.explanation: Everolimus binds the intracellular protein FKBP12; this complex inhibits mTORC1, affecting protein synthesis and growth signalling. This pathway can support endocrine resistance, which explains pairing it with an oestrogen-lowering medicine. The same pathway operates in normal tissues, contributing to mouth ulcers, infection risk and metabolic changes.
agents.watch: Report new mouth soreness, cough/breathlessness, fever/infection symptoms, diarrhoea or excessive thirst promptly. A new cough must not simply be labelled drug pneumonitis without checking other causes.
risks: Impaired wound healing and radiation-related toxicity

agents.name: Exemestane
agents.mechanism: Irreversibly inhibits aromatase and lowers oestrogen production
agents.explanation: After menopause, aromatase in tissues converts androgen precursors into oestrogen. Exemestane is an irreversible aromatase inhibitor that reduces this supply to hormone-sensitive cancer cells. It does not directly switch off functioning ovaries; the menopausal indication must be confirmed.
agents.watch: Tell the team if joint pain, hot flushes, vaginal dryness or sleep disturbance affects daily life. Bone thinning can be silent, so keep the agreed bone-health reviews.

urgent_extra: Contact the oncology team promptly for new or worsening cough or breathlessness, fever or infection symptoms, mouth sores that prevent drinking/eating, severe diarrhoea or dehydration, or marked thirst and frequent urination. Severe breathing difficulty, collapse or swelling of the tongue/throat needs emergency help.

sections.title: Before starting
sections.text: Confirm the exact medicine, strength, endocrine partner, baseline tests and first review appointments. Ask who arranges tests and who reviews the results.

sections.title: Taking treatment
sections.text: Take everolimus at the same time daily, consistently with food or consistently without food. Take exemestane after a meal. Swallow tablets whole with water; do not crush or chew. If a dose is missed, take the next scheduled dose without adding an extra dose.

sections.title: Treatment duration
sections.text: Continue while beneficial and tolerated; review each medicine separately if everolimus is held.

sections.title: Supply and appointments
sections.text: Request the next supply before tablets run out. Blood tests and any ECG or injections need their own appointments. This oral treatment does not itself require a central line or infusion pump.

sections.title: If treatment is held
sections.text: Ask which medicine is held, whether the endocrine partner continues, what needs to recover, when the next review is due and who will authorise restart.

sections.title: Support between appointments
sections.text: Keep the oncology contact details and prescribed symptom medicines accessible. New severe symptoms need prompt assessment rather than waiting for the next blood test.

evidence.title: BOLERO-2
evidence.intro: Studies describe groups. Ask how closely the treatment and study population match your situation.
evidence.population: Postmenopausal HR-positive/HER2-negative advanced breast cancer progressing during or after a non-steroidal aromatase inhibitor; 724 randomized patients.
evidence.interpretation: Adding everolimus to exemestane delayed cancer growth compared with exemestane alone in the study. The trial did not show a clear improvement in how long people lived overall. This older study cannot give a precise estimate for someone previously treated with modern CDK4/6 combinations.
evidence.limitations: Your team can discuss the strength and limitations of the evidence alongside treatment risks and alternatives.

teachback: Which medicine is taken when, which test is due next, who reviews it, and which symptoms mean you should call today?
consent_support: Discuss the treatment aim, alternatives, benefit and uncertainty, important medicine-specific risks, reproductive precautions, symptom support and planned duration. Confirm the endocrine partner and any ovarian-suppression plan. The timeline does not authorise a restart or certify clinical review.

support.title: Nausea support
support.text: Everolimus is oral minimal–low emetic risk. No routine infusion premedication is needed; agree individual rescue treatment and local oral-SACT advice.

support.title: Mouth care from the start
support.text: Agree non-alcoholic mouth care and whether a prescribed alcohol-free corticosteroid mouthwash is appropriate during the first eight weeks. Report mouth ulcers early and check for thrush rather than adding an antifungal automatically.

support.title: Lungs and infection
support.text: New cough, breathlessness or fever needs prompt review. If systemic steroids or other immunosuppression are used, the team considers PJP prevention according to risk.

support.title: Metabolic and bone health
support.text: Keep glucose, cholesterol, kidney and liver checks. Discuss diabetes/lipid care, exemestane bone risk, exercise, diet and any indicated bone-protection treatment.

support.title: Surgery, radiotherapy and other medicines
support.text: Tell both oncology and procedure teams about everolimus before surgery or radiotherapy. Check all new medicines and supplements; avoid grapefruit and St John’s wort.

questions.q: Do I need to enter dates?
questions.a: No. This map shows general timing without personal information. Your hospital arranges actual appointments; ask who books each test and who reviews its result.

questions.q: What if a dose is missed or treatment is held?
questions.a: Take everolimus at the same time daily, consistently with food or consistently without food. Take exemestane after a meal. Swallow tablets whole with water; do not crush or chew. If a dose is missed, take the next scheduled dose without adding an extra dose. A hold may affect one medicine rather than the whole combination; confirm each component.

questions.q: What happens after treatment changes or ends?
questions.a: Continue while beneficial and tolerated; review each medicine separately if everolimus is held. Keep the separately agreed disease follow-up, endocrine and bone-health plan.
